title: Editing fast
summary: F2, undo and redo, cut, copy, paste and Paste Special (values, formats, transpose).
objectives: Edit inside a cell with F2 instead of retyping it.
Undo and redo with the keyboard.
Use Paste Special for values, formats and transpose.

slides.h: Type over, or edit with F2
p: Typing into a cell **replaces** it. **F2** lets you edit what's already there.
**Delete** clears what's in a cell but keeps its formatting.
In edit mode, the arrow keys move inside the text.
In real life: Retyped a student's full name to fix one letter. With F2 he would have fixed just the letter.

p: Copy shows a moving dashed border. Paste as many times as you like.
**Ctrl+X** cuts: the cells move to where you paste.
Press **Esc** to clear the dashed border.
In real life: Copies the same vendor checklist into a new sheet for every wedding she manages.

check.q: A cell says “Ahmadabad”. What's the fastest way to fix it to “Ahmedabad”?
options: Delete the cell and retype it
Press F2 and change one letter
check.explain: **F2** opens the cell for editing, so you change just the one letter.

why.2: That replaces it with something else.
why.3: Paste Special chooses what to paste, not how to edit.

p: **Paste Special** (Ctrl+Alt+V) lets you choose which part of the copied cells to paste.
Right-click › Paste Special also opens it.
The normal Ctrl+V pastes everything: content, formulas and formats.
slides.say: **Paste Special** (Ctrl+Alt+V) lets you choose which part of the copied cells to paste.
points: Right-click › Paste Special also opens it.

terms: choose what to paste: values, formats…

p: A row becomes a column, or a column becomes a row.
Copy the range, click the first cell of the new spot, Paste Special › Transpose.
In real life: Receives monthly figures across a row but needs them down a column for a chart. One Transpose paste does it.

p: Paste **values** when you want the numbers but not the formulas behind them.
Sending a price list? Paste values so your formulas stay private.
Keep a copy of this month's totals before the data changes.
In real life: Sends clients quotes with values only, so they can't see how she worked out her margin.

check.explain: **Values** pastes the results only. The formulas stay in your own file.
